summary.thesis_claim: Proposed agent escalates with kill-chain context (higher confidence, correlation markers present); SOAR correctly mitigates on SID match but cannot escalate, correlate across stages, or distinguish cold vs. sequence.

reasoning: SID 9000001 detection: Suricata observed TCP SYN from 10.1.100.10 (WEB zone) to 10.1.200.10:5432 (DB-OLTP zone) — this is a hard microsegmentation violation per threat playbook.
Baseline verification: Flow 'WEB → DB-OLTP on port 5432' does NOT exist in production traffic baselines. Legitimate path is WEB→APP-GW→APP-CORE→DB-OLTP only.

Asset criticality assessment: Source web-01 is high-criticality (public-facing attack surface), destination db-oltp-01 is crown-jewel (transactional data). Direct access bypasses all defense-in-depth controls.
MITRE mapping: Alert maps to TA0008 Lateral Movement / T1021 Remote Services — attacker attempting to pivot from Internet-exposed tier to sensitive data tier.
Historical precedent: Past 90-day lookback shows 1 exact-SID incident (2026-06-01) with enforced DROP action, plus 2 semantically-similar incidents (SID 9000002) — pattern is recurring threat.
Trust score analysis: Source 10.1.100.10 has trust score 0.2 with 2 prior alerts (SID 9000002, SID 9000001) — host shows repeated policy-violation behavior.
Targeted block selection: Chose src+dst+port specific DROP (not full-source block) to preserve legitimate web-to-appgw-proxy flow (criticality=critical) while stopping the violation.
Confidence calibration: 0.95 — unambiguous policy violation with zero legitimate runtime scenarios, corroborated by historical enforcement pattern and MITRE technique match.

hypotheses.name: Lateral movement attempt
hypotheses.description: Lateral movement attempt (probability=0.95) — Compromised web-01 attempting direct database access, bypassing the required WEB→APP-GW→APP-CORE→DB chain. Evidence: SID 9000001 triggered on TCP SYN to PostgreSQL port 5432; flow not in any production baseline; source zone WEB (untrusted) to destination DB-OLTP (crown-jewel); past enforcement history shows this pattern was blocked before. Counter: None - this is a hard policy violation with zero legitimate runtime use case.

hypotheses.name: Misconfigured monitoring tool
hypotheses.description: Misconfigured monitoring tool (probability=0.04) — Monitoring agent incorrectly configured to scrape DB metrics from web host. Evidence: None in alert context. Counter: Monitoring traffic should originate from MONITORING zone (10.4.200.0/24), not WEB; no prior incidents of this FP pattern.

hypotheses.name: Pre-announced DB migration script
hypotheses.description: Pre-announced DB migration script (probability=0.01) — Emergency schema change executed from web host. Evidence: None. Counter: DB migrations should originate from MGT zone via change management process; would be pre-communicated in change window; no such notification in context.
